chunks: Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: My grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to me, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sukuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both)

He said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and asked him: Why is it that I do not love death? He said to him: Do you have wealth? He said: Yes. He said: Have you sent it ahead (of you)? He said: No. He said: Then that is why you do not love death.

key_terms.قَدَّمْتَهُ: Have you sent it ahead (of you)

ai.seo_question: Why does attachment to worldly wealth cause a person to dislike death?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal highlights the psychological barrier of material attachment to the afterlife, a key theme in Shia eschatology regarding the 'preparation' of one's soul. The Prophet’s diagnostic question reveals that the aversion to death stems not from fear of the unknown, but from the retention of worldly wealth that has not been converted into spiritual capital through charity or good deeds. This narrative underscores the practical necessity of purifying one's assets to facilitate a smooth transition to the barzakh.
